title: On the minimum number of maximal distance-$k$ independent sets in trees
summary: A vertex subset of a graph is called a distance-$k$ independent set if the distance between any two of its distinct vertices is at least $k + 1$. For all $n,k \geq 1$, we determine the minimum possible number of inclusion-wise maximal distance-$k$ independent sets among all $n$-vertex trees. It equals $n$ if $n \leq k + 1$, and $n - \bigg\lfloor \frac{n - (k \bmod 2)}{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor + 1} \bigg\rfloor + 1$ otherwise.
